children: India's central bank has attracted $143.6 billion in inflows under its forex swap facility as of September 18, data released on Monday showed.

In June, the Reserve Bank of India introduced a set of measures, including concessional hedging facilities and swap arrangements aimed at attracting foreign currency to shore up the rupee, which fell to record lows earlier this year.
Foreign currency non-resident, or FCNR(B), deposits accounted for the bulk of inflows, at $132.98 billion as of August 31, after the window was closed earlier than planned following robust inflows.
Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings contributed $5.32 billion and External Commercial Borrowings added $5.30 billion, RBI said.
Borrowings raised via ECBs and OFCBs will continue to be eligible under the swap facility until December 31

In times of currency stress, India has often relied on its diaspora for dollar deposits, offering subsidies on hedging costs as an incentive. The scheme was last used in 2013 and attracted about $26 billion.
